summary.intent: Improve memory quality in the memory-loop pipeline by adding a hard evidence gate that requires generated memories to be backed by repeated, verifiable signals from the pattern analysis phase. Also fix several UX issues with the summary command (slow startup, missing facets, wrong branch filter default).
summary.outcome: Implemented a two-layer evidence gate in the memory generator that requires provenance via source_signal and session ID validation against PatternAnalysis signals. Fixed summary command to not auto-backfill on load, fixed JSON parsing failures in facet/improve/memoryloop generators, and fixed the summary TUI branch filter to default to current branch with 'repo' meaning all branches.

repo: The memory generator's 'stability' was enforced only via LLM prompt instruction, not code — passesReviewDerivedGate was the only hard gate and only applied to review-derived rules
PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions uses CheckpointID not SessionID — identifier mismatch was a prerequisite to fix before implementing session validation
improve/analyzer.go filtered out skill opportunities with count < 2 before they reached the generator, making the singleton exception for skill_patch records unreachable
The summary command ran BackfillSummaries and BackfillFacets unconditionally on every invocation, causing 20+ sequential LLM calls on first load with no progress output

All three LLM JSON parsers (memoryloop/generator.go, facets/facets.go, improve/generator.go) used raw json.Unmarshal without handling trailing text after the JSON object, causing silent parse failures
repo_learning and workflow_learning in PatternAnalysis are plain []string without counts or AffectedSessions, making them ineligible as source_signal types
The 'repo' branch filter in summary TUI was filtering to defaultBranch (main/master) but no sessions exist on main — sessions are on feature branches
llmcli.Runner.Execute applies ExtractJSONFromMarkdown which handles ```json blocks but not trailing natural language text after bare JSON objects

code.finding: Prompt instruction 'Avoid one-off incidents without repeated evidence' is LLM guidance only, not enforced
SourceSessionIDs was captured but never validated for length — a 1-session record was treated identically to a 5-session record
passesReviewDerivedGate enforced count >= 2 || strong but only for review-derived rules, not repo_rule, workflow_rule, or agent_instruction kinds
if acc.count < 2 { continue } filtered skill opportunities before generator, making singleton exception unreachable
BackfillSummaries and BackfillFacets called unconditionally on every summary command invocation, writing to io.Discard
json.Unmarshal on raw LLM response without extractJSONObject fallback caused silent facet extraction failures when LLM added trailing text
filterRepo filtered to defaultBranch (main/master) but no sessions existed there; should mean all branches

workflow: When adding a hard gate that relies on LLM-provided fields, cross-reference against upstream analysis data you already trust rather than trusting the LLM's output alone
Before implementing a cross-reference approach, verify that identifier types are consistent end-to-end (CheckpointID vs SessionID)
Move shared utility functions to jsonutil package rather than duplicating across packages
LLMs frequently add trailing text after JSON even when prompted 'Return ONLY JSON' — always have a fallback that extracts the outermost balanced {} pair

friction: The existing passesReviewDerivedGate pattern worked via a dedicated review-rule field, not general provenance — this made extending the pattern to other signal types non-trivial
PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions used CheckpointID while the generator prompt exposed SessionID — identifier alignment was a blocker that required fixing the prompt
The memory generator JSON parse error ('invalid character n after top-level value') required two separate debug cycles because the binary wasn't rebuilt after the first fix
Many existing tests had to be updated to include SourceSignal provenance after the evidence gate was added
The branch filter removal-then-restoration required multiple roundtrips to understand that 'repo' should mean 'all branches' not 'main branch'
Removing defaultBranch from RunWithCurrentBranch signature required fixing callsites in summary_cmd.go, summary_cmd_test.go, and root_test.go with several missed occurrences
open_items: The matchedSignal type definition was added to the code but the doc sketch didn't fully define it — the implementation resolved this but the doc could be more precise
improve/generator.go and summarize/claude.go may have additional JSON parse failure modes not yet investigated
The full CI test suite was still running when the transcript ended — final test results not confirmed
No backfill mechanism for existing low-quality memories already in memory-loop.json — natural decay handles it but no explicit cleanup path
repo_learning and workflow_learning lines still fed to LLM in prompt even though they're ineligible for source_signal — marked as context-only but still waste tokens
implementation_rationale: Used source_signal provenance (Layer 1) + session ID validation against signal.AffectedSessions (Layer 2) instead of just checking SourceSessionIDs length, because LLM-provided session IDs can be hallucinated or padded
Extended passesReviewDerivedGate pattern to all signal types via matchedSignal.AllowsSingleton rather than adding per-kind special cases

Reject-by-default fallback at both layers (no matching signal = hard reject) rather than allow-if-unmatched, because the bad cases being eliminated are precisely the ones that won't map to repeated signals
Added matchedSignal.Kind field to prevent singleton exception from leaking to wrong record kinds (e.g., repo_rule record matching a skill_opportunity signal inheriting AllowsSingleton=true)
Moved extractJSONObject to jsonutil package to avoid duplicating across memoryloop, facets, and improve packages
Kept isLiteralReviewEvidence as a standalone pre-gate check to preserve the verbatim review comment rejection behavior that was previously inside passesReviewDerivedGate
Lowered skill opportunity analyzer threshold from count >= 2 to count >= 1 so the evidence gate's singleton exception for skill_patch records is actually reachable
Removed auto-backfill from summary command entirely rather than making it lazy or showing progress, per user's explicit requirement that backfill should only happen on user request
tradeoffs: Hard gate on source_signal provenance means cold-start scenarios (new repo, first occurrence of a real pattern) get rejected — accepted tradeoff for quality
Exact normalized match with substring fallback for findSignal — exact is safer (fewer false positives) but rejects valid records where LLM paraphrased the key

Two-filter layers: provenance gate alone isn't sufficient because LLM could fabricate a valid-looking source_signal key; session ID validation against AffectedSessions provides the second independent check
Removing auto-backfill means sessions start with no summaries/facets — users must press 'g' per session instead of getting background population
Singleton exception for skill_patch records allows one-time skill discoveries through while blocking other one-off memories
codebase_patterns: GenerationStats struct tracks filter counts (FilteredWeakCount, FilteredGenericCount) and is propagated to RefreshHistory and displayed in memory_loop_cmd.go
Evidence gate pattern follows the existing passesReviewDerivedGate structure: per-kind signal lookup + count threshold + singleton allowlist
LLM calls use llmcli.Runner.Execute which already applies ExtractJSONFromMarkdown for code block stripping, but not trailing text stripping
PatternAnalysis signal types with counts: RepeatedInstructions, FailureLoops, SkillOpportunities, ReviewDerivedRules — repo_learning/workflow_learning are plain []string without counts
Test stubs use package-level function vars (e.g., runSummaryTUI, summaryBackfillSummaries) for injectable mocking
jsonutil package holds shared JSON utilities for the CLI
